current_activity: The Twenty-fourth Army, a deception name for headquarters troops on the Swiss frontier, crosses Lake Constance by boat
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 434: "a force of little more than division size deceptively called the"; "The Twenty-fourth Army had escaped the French trap by crossing Lake Constance by boat". Event definition: CMH gives no day; the escape belongs to the French advance to the lake of 21 April, so the date is approximate. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Lake Constance, northwestern end (representative point at Überlingen) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: Überlingen stands for the lake crossing; the headquarters place is not named. Location support: CMH names Lake Constance for the crossing. Commander: General der Infanterie Hans Schmidt. Opponents: First French Army.

current_activity: Schmidt asks the French for surrender terms for the Twenty-fourth Army at noon on 4 May; the terms are then disputed
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 19 p. 472: "General der Infanterie Hans Schmidt, had approached the French at noon on 4 May with a request for terms of surrender"; p. 473: "only French troops faced the Twenty-fourth Army". Event definition: the request at noon on 4 May; the dispute over the terms continued to 6 May. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Bregenz, Vorarlberg with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: Bregenz, on Lake Constance at the Swiss and Austrian frontier, stands for the army area; CMH names no town. Location support: CMH says only that the army faced French troops at the Swiss frontier. Commander: General der Infanterie Hans Schmidt. Opponents: First French Army.
